title: Consolidated solution: orchestration by scripts, a smaller plugin, a simpler CI
description: Holds the work the owner's 2026-10-14 decisions (D1-D10 of the cost/code/CI synthesis, quality-gates-internal reports/2026-10-14-cost-code-ci-analysis) moved out of P125 until the segment studies (orchestration, code, CI) produce one consolidated plan. Its tasks are re-planned from those studies before any starts.
desiredOutcome: A task through the plugin costs about 1.25x a plain session above a measured size threshold, the main loop reads one signal line per step, scripts+hooks shrink toward 115k lines with code not above its 3.4.0 count, and CI runs in at most 8 minutes from one executable description of the gate set.

tasks.title: A red CI run on a phase's ci/ branch files a manifest bug with its failing jobs and cases
tasks.description: Observed 2026-10-12: ci/p122 (run 38017386858) and ci/p124 (run 38036907164) went red on windows-latest two days before the 3.3.0 cut, yet no task or bug was filed, P123 landed on top, and the release candidate's CI (38299118105) found nine Windows files red - all new in P123, none overlapping P124's bt2/sr210 which P123 had fixed. The per-phase CI ran as intended; its verdict reached no record a gate reads. A CI result is read into the plan: a command (or the drive's landing step, once it has pushed ci/<phase>) reads the run's failing jobs and case ids (`gh run view --log-failed`, parsed by the house FAIL/FAILED reader) and files `/audit:bug add` naming the run, the jobs and each failing case, so the release guard and the open-bug rule see it at once. Refuses rather than files when it cannot read the run. Source: testbed monitor, 2026-10-12.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_drive_phase.py: a recorded red CI run for a phase's ci/ branch files one bug naming the run id, each failing job and each failing case id; an unreadable run is refused, not filed empty

tasks.title: A long phase dispatches CI on its branch at a configured cadence, not only at landing
tasks.description: P123 ran about 2.5 days and about 90 tasks with no CI run between its start and its landing, so nine windows-latest regressions it introduced surfaced only at the 3.3.0 cut (run 38299118105) and cost a fix phase (P126). The drive already pushes ci/ branches; give it a cadence: `ci.cadence` in config (every N task closes and/or every H hours of phase time, absent = landing only), on which it pushes the phase tip to ci/<phase> and dispatches the workflow without waiting, and reads the result at the next close; a red files a bug through ci-red-files-bug. Doctor reports the setting. Source: testbed monitor, 2026-10-12.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_drive_phase.py: with ci.cadence every 3 closes the drive dispatches CI on the third close and not before, never waits on it, and reads its verdict at the next close; absent, it dispatches only at landing

tasks.title: Phase review can run Haiku-first and escalate on a computed predicate, off by default
tasks.description: N2. Config review.cascade: 'off' (default) | 'haiku-first'. When on, dispatch_phase_review dispatches the reviewer with model=claude-haiku-5-5 and the same brief and JSON return; a pure predicate escalate(filed, phase) decides whether a second, Sonnet dispatch is owed: any finding, any cannot-tell or missing intent input, any recorded open choice, red-first not proved, or an existing test file modified (the signals signals_fired() and the brief already compute). The second filing supersedes the first in _filed_returns, and both are kept in evidence with their model. The predicate's verdict per phase is computed offline over the recorded phase fixtures and printed by a selftest; the cascade's false-negative rate needs model calls and is not measured here (openChoices), which is why the default is off. Depends on the price table so a Haiku dispatch is priced, not _default. Evidence (research report 2026-10-12, probe 2): Haiku matched Opus on the target defect at about 1/18 of the cost ONLY under the clause-quoting rule of intent-against-task-text; one scenario, false-positive rate not measured - so this depends on that task and its predicate must be re-measured before default-on.

tasks.title: A task's scope gains the follower files its changes owe, derived from the lints
tasks.description: Sketch section 0: declared scope is exact-path and append-only, so tasks widened for followers mid-run. Each lint that requires a companion edit exposes its rule as data next to its own check, built from the constants it already reads: _deps (a new .py under scripts/ or hooks/ owes _deps.py's LAYERS, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's tree line and section, tests/test__output.py; an import change owes the guide's module-map fence), _output (a new scripts/ .py owes the path preamble - in-file, so no follower), _refs (a version bump owes the README pins), tools/prove-gates.py and tools/gate-parity.py (a new lint owes their rows). tools/followers.py collects these rules and prints them as JSON lines for a path set. The product side: a pure _followers module reads rules from the project's meta.followers.command plus the generic companions in openChoices, and audit-task add, scope and add --fixes append the followers to files with a printed basis per added path (never silently). Each repo rule is proven true rather than claimed: a selftest builds a fixture where the follower is omitted and asserts the owning lint goes red.

tasks.title: Dispatch prompts and briefs put the stable text first and the task-specific text last
tasks.description: Sketch section 3. A subagent's cached prefix ends where its task message starts to differ, and today the main loop composes each dispatch prompt itself from the driver's one-line instruction. drive-phase prints the exact prompt to send for each role, as one fixed sentence per role followed by the variable part (task id, brief path) last, and the orchestrator reference says to send it verbatim; audit-lookup orders each brief file's sections stable-first (the role's rules and return contract before the task's description, files and diff). Measure, do not claim: tools/stream-cost.py's dispatches reading (startRead/startWritten) on a recorded session is the basis for any figure, and measure-context's INSTRUCTION_BYTES and AGENT_CEILINGS must still hold.

tasks.title: An executor or reviewer reply longer than its filed line is sent back once
tasks.description: F567: 'hand back the line above as your whole reply' is printed by submit and followed by no executor (measured hand-backs ran to kilobytes). A new SubagentStop hook, scoped by agent_type to the plugin's executor and reviewer: submit writes the line it printed to the state dir keyed by the task id the agent's meta description starts with; the hook compares last_assistant_message to that line and, when the reply is longer, returns decision block once with the line as the reason, so the agent's final message - the one the main loop carries - becomes that line. It blocks at most once per agent (a marker per agent_id) and is fail-open: no line on file, an unreadable payload or a non-plugin agent passes. Confirm the payload fields with a probe before relying on them (the hooks reference documents last_assistant_message on SubagentStop). Register it in hooks.json, keep it inside tools/bench-hooks.py's import budget, and list it in SECURITY.md's fail-open table. Also (F574): stream-cost apportions a rebuilt final's output over the whole tool-result bytes, counting the CLI's frame and trailer as emitted - subtract the frame and trailer before apportioning, and switch pipeline-cost-design.md's ad-hoc `analyse(load_events(...))` commands to the CLI so they meet its refusal of a follow-up stream read alone. Faults add: F574.

tasks.title: CI fails when a recorded session's reconstructed cost exceeds its ceiling
tasks.description: Sketch section 3. tools/stream-cost.py gains --gate: for each committed recording it reconstructs per-stage cost (main loop, executor, reviewer, hand-back) at the shipped table and fails on any stage above its ceiling, printing stage, figure, ceiling and pricing basis; an unpriced model fails the gate as unpriced rather than counting zero. Recordings are committed redacted (see openChoices): a redaction mode keeps counts, model ids, tool names and byte lengths and replaces text, and check-committed-pii must pass over them. Wire the gate into tools/verify.sh and .github/workflows/ci.yml, describe it in CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md's test list, add its gate-parity entry and its prove-gates row (raising a recording's cost above the ceiling must go red; a recording at the ceiling must stay green).

tasks.title: The phase cycle as a plugin Workflow has a design and an offline measurement
tasks.description: N3, design and measurement only - no implementation, because the decisive facts (hooks firing inside workflow-spawned agents, the stagger's cache read, the main loop's real saving) need a paid probe. Write the design: run-phase.js's stages, the Haiku runner that calls drive-phase next and returns {exit, print} by schema, the on-disk token the script must re-read so a mis-relayed print cannot mis-route the loop, how every decide ends the run (workflows take no mid-run input), the fallback to today's Agent path for orgs with workflows off, the Claude Code version floor for COMPATIBILITY.md, and the guarantees to re-argue (gate independence, plan gate inside workflow agents, nothing owed to a human lands unseen). Measure offline with tools/stream-cost.py on recorded sessions: the main loop's spend between dispatches and the hand-back rows, each figure beside the command that produced it. End with the paid probe's exact protocol and the readings that would accept or reject the design.

tasks.title: A task's model follows its recorded complexity as well as its risk, with the reason shown before approval
tasks.description: F634 (owner-raised, measured on the testbed): `audit-task._model_floor` routes opus only for `risk: high`, and risk is blast radius, not difficulty - nearly every testbed task ran on Sonnet, including the plan's hardest code (an astronomy core, a WebGL sky layer), because each was low risk; no planning step asks about difficulty. (1) A task records `complexity` (low/med/high) with a one-line basis, separate from risk, written by planning (init synthesis, `/audit:phase add`, `audit-task add`/`scope`) and validated by the manifest schema and rules (additive: a plan without it stays valid and reads as unrecorded, never defaulted). (2) Routing: opus when risk is high OR complexity is high, else sonnet; the caller's explicit `--model` still wins; a config key (`executor.modelByComplexity`, documented in COMPATIBILITY.md as added) can turn the complexity arm off. (3) The plan preview and `/audit:status` show each task's model and the reason it was chosen (risk, complexity, or the caller). (4) Escalation: after a retry, or a med+ finding on a Sonnet attempt, the next attempt of that task runs on opus, journaled with the reason. Red-first: two low-risk fixture tasks - a WebGL scene marked complexity high and a copy edit marked low - route to opus and sonnet; a retried Sonnet task's next dispatch names opus and the journal row says why. Faults: F634.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: a low-risk task with complexity high routes to opus and one with complexity low to sonnet; an explicit --model wins; a plan without complexity stays valid and reads as unrecorded
plugins/audit/tests/test_drive_phase.py: after a retry on a sonnet attempt the next dispatch names opus and the journal row records why

tasks.title: Parallel waves respect a shared external-resource budget: resources in config, needs on a task, and status says why a task was held
tasks.description: F508 (deferred feature; its revisit trigger - a waves verb - has fired with P124's waves). Today parallel safety is disjoint `files` plus `dependsOn` only, so two tasks that each start a dev server on one port, or hit one rate-limited API, run side by side (the testbed's port 3100 collision is the live shape). Add `resources: {name: capacity}` to audit.config.json (schema + config rules, additive, documented in COMPATIBILITY.md), `needs: [name]` on a task (plan schema + rules, additive), cap wave membership where waves are computed so a wave never holds more tasks needing a resource than its capacity, and have status/the drive say which task was held and for which resource. In the scheduler, not in executor prose. Red-first: two ready tasks both needing `port3100` with capacity 1 never share a wave, the held one is named with the resource; without `resources` the waves are unchanged. Faults: F508.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__status_facts.py: two ready tasks needing one capacity-1 resource never share a wave and the held one names the resource; no resources config leaves waves unchanged
